subject: Canary safety net — pin-and-failover plan for FastPay deployment
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@fastpay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops-eng@fastpay.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Canary window + SLA impact question

Hi Marissa,

Quick question as we finalize cutover dates: our platform requires a short canary (48hr) for the payments flow. Legal/ops have flagged Redwood's standard uptime SLA during staged launches and asked whether we can get formal language that documents what will happen if latency increases or an availability regression occurs during the canary.

Specifically: can Redwood commit to an automatic failback to the previous pinned model/instance and guarantee no SLA credits will be applied while we run the approved canary if the failback triggers? If not, what exception language or operational safeguards do you propose so our procurement team can sign off?

We need something brief to show our procurement team by Wednesday.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Platform Operations | FastPay
[Attachment: fastpay_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fastpay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Canary window + SLA impact question

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can propose a carveout that preserves your SLA exposure during an agreed canary period provided the canary follows a set of telemetry gates and an automated rollback policy. Below is a concise plan we can include in contract language; happy to convert to a one‑page exhibit for procurement.

High-level proposal (for procurement exhibit):
- Canary window: 48 hours (as requested).
- Traffic shepherding: start at 1% and step to 5% / 15% / 50% over the first 8 hours, then monitor for the remainder of the window.
- Telemetry gates (failure if any trigger):
  * P50 / P95 latency regressions > 40% over baseline for 30m window
  * Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute for 15m window
  * Token-level throughput drop outside expected variance with no concurrent capacity events
- Automated action: on gate failure, the platform will auto‑pin to the last known stable model/instance and route 100% traffic to it within the next 90s (automatic failback).
- SLA handling: the carveout states that SLA credit calculations will exclude the canary window provided the customer ran an agreed canary per the runbook and the failback executed according to the automated policy (i.e., rollback occurred within the 90s window). If a manual override delays failback beyond the automated window, normal SLA terms apply.
- Evidence: full audit trail (timestamped routing change, telemetry graphs, and runbook execution logs) will be provided via the Redwood Console export and a signed runbook acceptance.

Attachments: I attached a short runbook outline and a draft SLA carveout PDF for your procurement team to review.

If this aligns with FastPay's needs I can loop legal to produce the one‑page exhibit and a DocuSign link.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: canary-runbook.md (text)] [Attachment: fastpay-sla-carveout.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 10:00:00 -05:00
Subject: Internal: FastPay SLA carveout — approve language?

Laura / Ben — looping you in to get signoff on the proposed canary carveout for FastPay (deal FP-2026-049). Customer asked for procurement-ready language by Wednesday. Key asks below; ping me if you want a quick call.

Summary of proposal (short):
- 48hr canary; automated rollback to previous pinned variant within 90s on gate failure; SLA credits excluded during canary if the automated failback executed within 90s and customer followed runbook.

Risks / thumb rules:
- We must ensure rollback automation is tested in the FastPay staging account prior to production canary.
- Avoid open manual approvals in the middle of the canary window (manual delays void carveout).
- Legal prefers: (a) explicit telemetry thresholds, (b) evidence retention for 12 months.

Can you reply with: 1) approval to send to legal & FastPay, or 2) edits to the thresholds or the 90s SLA on failback?

Thanks — I attached the draft carveout and runbook.

Marissa
[Attachment: fastpay-sla-carveout.pdf] [Attachment: canary-runbook.md]

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@fastpay.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops-eng@fastpay.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:32:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Canary window + SLA impact question

Marissa — this looks good and clears the main procurement concern. A few quick notes from legal/ops:
- Please include the exact telemetry thresholds in the exhibit (you already listed them; we want them verbatim).
- FastPay requests that the evidence export be a signed PDF delivered within 5 business days after any rollback event.
- Can you send the DocuSign link for the carveout exhibit?

If you can share the link and send a staging smoke test schedule we can confirm the production canary for next Monday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Platform Operations | FastPay
[Attachment: ops_questions.txt (text)]
